Radio Iowa, April 16, 2001: 'Governor Tom Vilsack has declared 10 Iowa counties along the Mississippi River state disaster areas' as record or near-record flooding was predicted. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Radio Iowa, June 5, 2002: 'The Governor declared seven flooded eastern Iowa counties disaster areas yesterday afternoon' (June 4).

Radio Iowa, May 24, 2004: Governor Tom Vilsack 'has now declared 17 counties disaster areas', adding Floyd County that morning, after tornadoes and flooding swept the state over the weekend. The first counties were declared earlier and the story does not give that day, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, March 1, 2007: 'Governor Chet Culver has now declared the entire state a disaster area', adding 39 counties to the 60 declared after the first winter storm. The day of the first 60-county proclamation is not given.

Radio Iowa, May 7, 2007: 'Governor Chet Culver issued a Governor's Emergency Proclamation Sunday' (May 6) for Harrison, Pottawattamie and Montgomery counties; Decatur and Fremont were added the next day.

Radio Iowa, August 22, 2007: 'Iowa Governor Chet Culver declared five north-central and north-west Iowa counties state disasters areas' after heavy rains produced flooding; the proclamation covers Boone, Humboldt, Palo Alto, Pocahontas and Webster. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, December 14, 2007: 'The governor has declared 22 counties state disaster areas' after the ice storm, and the proclamation allows state resources to be used. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, May 26, 2008: 'Governor Chet Culver issued a state disaster proclamation for Blackhawk, Butler Counties' after the May 25 tornado. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, December 29, 2009: 'The governor has declared a state of emergency for four western Iowa counties' and issued the disaster proclamation so DOT crews can help clear snow from the Christmas storm. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, January 22, 2010: 'Governor Chet Culver has issued emergency proclamations for Carroll, Cass, Crawford and Sac Counties' to get state help after the ice storm. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Radio Iowa, June 29, 2010: 'Governor Chet Culver today doubled the number of counties under a state disaster proclamation', adding 14 counties for storms and flooding to 14 proclaimed earlier.

CNN, reprinted April 10, 2011: the tornado that hit Mapleton on Saturday night (April 9) was enough to 'prompt Iowa Gov. Terry E. Branstad to issue a disaster proclamation in Monona County'. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, June 2, 2011: 'The proclamation covers Fremont, Harrison, Mills, Monona, Pottawattamie and Woodbury counties' for the Missouri River flooding. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, July 19, 2011: 'Governor Branstad issued emergency disaster proclamations last week for Benton, Tama, Marshall and Story Counties' after the storms. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Radio Iowa, April 19, 2013: 'Governor Terry Branstad today issued a disaster proclamation' for five eastern Iowa counties after storms and flooding that began April 17.

Radio Iowa, May 29, 2013: 'Governor Branstad issued disaster proclamations for 13 Iowa counties following recent storms and flooding.' The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Radio Iowa, June 4, 2014: 'Late Tuesday, Governor Branstad issued a proclamation of disaster for Pottawattamie County as a result of storm damage' (June 3).
Radio Iowa, June 18, 2014: 'Late Tuesday afternoon Governor Branstad declared disaster emergencies in five counties' (June 17).

Radio Iowa, July 2, 2014: the governor's office said 'disaster proclamations have been issued for 51 counties in the past month following severe storms on June 3rd, 13th and 26th'. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, June 24, 2015: 'Governor Branstad issued a disaster proclamation for Davis, Humboldt, Monroe and Wright counties' after the storms. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, August 26, 2016: 'Governor Terry Branstad has declared Allamakee, Clayton, Fayette, Howard and Winneshiek counties state disaster areas in response to the severe storms and flash flooding.' The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

The proclamation as posted by FMCSA, effective September 23, 2016: Gov. Branstad 'formally issued a proclamation of disaster emergency for 13 counties in response to recent flooding' after storms beginning September 21. Radio Iowa reported the signing the same day.

Radio Iowa, July 24, 2017: 'The governor issued a disaster proclamation for Bremer, Buchanan, Clinton and Johnson counties' for the July 21-22 flash flooding, after earlier proclamations for Allamakee, Clayton, Fayette and Winneshiek. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, June 11, 2018: 'The governor has approved disaster proclamations for seven counties in response to severe weather and flooding that started June 7th.' The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Radio Iowa, July 20, 2018: after Thursday's tornado outbreak, 'the governor issued a disaster proclamation for Marshall County'. The story does not give the day the proclamation was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Albert Lea Tribune, March 14, 2019: Iowa's governor signed an emergency proclamation for 21 counties on Thursday (March 14) as river flooding from rainfall and snowmelt continued.
